title: Iran strikes US base; mines hit tankers in Hormuz
detail: Iran struck a US helicopter base in Bahrain on 15 Nov; on 16 Nov the Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and state TV said five vessels were hit. Oil fell anyway: Brent is below $92 as the IEA sees a ~2 mb/d surplus this quarter, and Saudi Arabia and the UAE cut selling prices. Trump says more strikes may not be needed.
countries: SA JP KR IN CN TR IT EA
implication: The market is betting supply outruns the conflict. A sustained Hormuz closure is the tail risk for importers (JP, KR, IN, TR, IT); a glut squeezes producers (SA, RU).

title: Fed: December hike ~92% priced; 10-year at 5.14%
detail: October CPI +0.4% m/m and PPI +6.5% y/y. December hike odds rose to ~92% (25bp). The 10-year jumped ~30bp last week and the dollar index is at a 19-month high. Chair Warsh speaks 16 Nov; FOMC minutes on 18 Nov.
countries: US TR ZA BR AR IN ID
implication: Higher US yields and a strong dollar tighten conditions for dollar borrowers and long-duration stocks; EM currencies (lira, rand, real, peso) are most exposed.

title: AI sell-off deepens before Nvidia results
detail: The S&P 500 fell 1.9% on 16 Nov and the VIX jumped 19% to 22.9 as the AI unwind continued after Jensen Huang's exit; Nvidia has fallen six straight weeks. Funds are selling bonds to raise cash, and copper hit its lowest since June. Results due after the close on 17 Nov.
implication: The biggest single-stock risk to the AI capex cycle; Korea and Japan equities and AI-linked corporate bonds carry the most exposure.

title: France slides toward recession
detail: Composite PMI 46.6 (September 51.1), services 46.2; Q3 GDP −0.1% q/q and industrial output −1.3% y/y.
implication: French banks and domestic cyclicals; OAT-Bund spread is the stress gauge.

title: Japan Q3 GDP flat, below forecasts
detail: Q3 GDP 0.0% q/q (−0.1% annualised) vs +0.1% expected. Yen near 159 per dollar.
implication: Weak growth and a weak yen leave the BoJ squeezed; intervention risk is high near 160.

title: China October data miss: output 4.8%, retail sales 0.4%
detail: Industrial production +4.8% y/y vs 5.3% expected; retail sales +0.4% vs 0.8% expected (autos −21.4%); October exports fell to $412bn and refinery throughput dropped.
implication: Weak China demand weighs on iron ore, copper and soy exporters (AU, BR) and Korean suppliers; raises odds of more stimulus.

title: BoE: December hike ~82% priced
detail: The BoE warned inflation could rise from 3.5% to ~5% by mid-2027; December hike odds rose to 82% from 50% a week earlier. Gilt yields rose.
implication: Gilts, housebuilders and UK consumer stocks carry the downside with consumer confidence at −24.

title: India inflation breaks the RBI's 6% ceiling
detail: October CPI 6.09% from 5.54% (food 8.94%), the first breach of the 6% band since Oct 2024; the October trade gap widened to $39.9bn.
implication: Raises odds of another RBI hike; pressure on the rupee and rate-sensitive Indian stocks.

title: RBA hiked into a slowing economy
detail: RBA raised the cash rate to 4.85% (6–3), an 18-year high, with the composite PMI at 48.2. Consumer confidence fell to 78.2 in November; the AUD hit a 9-month low.
implication: Banks, housing and consumer stocks carry the downside.

title: Brazil business confidence slumps
detail: Business confidence fell to 40.2 from 46.2 in November after a 44.4 composite PMI. The real fell past 5.65 per dollar on a fiscal bill seen as too timid.
implication: Selic cuts become the question; BRL and local bonds are the pressure points.

title: Euro-area inflation at 4.0%
detail: October CPI 4.0% from 3.8%; Italy 5.4%. Euro-area Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q, retail sales +0.4% y/y.
implication: ECB hike bias persists while growth slows; periphery spreads widen first.

title: Copper stocks swell ahead of US tariffs
detail: LME copper stocks ~320,000t from 205,000t in August as metal is diverted to the US before possible import tariffs; copper at a four-month low near $6.0/lb.
implication: Tariff front-running is distorting copper signals; a weak price partly reflects China demand.

title: UK grew 0.7% in Q3
detail: In line with forecasts, led by services. Backward-looking after the BoE hike.

title: Baltic Dry snaps a 7-day run
detail: Down 1.3% to 2,980; still +12% on the month.

title: Gold at its lowest since Oct 2025
detail: Near $3,850 on a strong dollar and higher yields.

title: Anthropic IPO expected this week
detail: Reportedly heavily oversubscribed. Market sentiment item, not a macro signal.
